contests.note: PREVIOUSLY UNVERIFIED, AND THE FLAG WAS DOING ITS JOB. This record was carried with bands: [] and eligibility guessed as ZS-only 'Confirm', because sarl.org.za served an expired certificate. SARL has since moved to mysarl.org.za and the rules are now readable: the recurrence and times the record already held were right, the bands are 20/40/80 m, and the eligibility guess was WRONG -- the scoring table's Area 9 is 'Stations in the rest of the world'. log_deadline_days is 5, which is the right DAY and not the right hour: SARL states 'by 21:59 UTC on Friday', and the contest ends at 17:00 UTC on the Sunday five days before, so the engine's derived log_due lands at 17:00 rather than 21:59. contests.name: All Asian DX Contest, CW
contests.exchange: RS(T) and the operator's age. An operator who does not want to send an age sends 01. Multi-operator stations send the average age of the operators at the start of the contest.
contests.source_note: jarl.org (67th All Asian DX Contest rule): 'CW: (June 20-21,2026) From 00:00 UTC on the third Saturday in June to 24:00 UTC on the following day'. Bands: 'Amateur bands 160m, 80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m'. Power: 'Low Power: Total output power must not exceed 100 watts. High Power: There is no limitation on total output power within the maximum allowable power level established by the national licensing authority'. The third Saturday in June 2026 is June 20, which is the date JARL prints. LOG DEADLINE DELIBERATELY NOT ENCODED: JARL states 'Logs must arrive at JARL no later than 10 days after the event is over. CW...July 1, 2026'. July 1 is 10 days after the last contest DAY (June 21), not 10 days after the 24:00 UTC end instant this record stores, so log_deadline_days would have to be 9 to reproduce JARL's own date. Rather than print a number JARL never wrote, the rule is quoted here and the field is omitted. Logs also go to aacw@jarl.org.
contests.summary: JARL's CW leg of the All Asian DX Contest: 24 hours over the third weekend in June, exchanging signal report and the operator's age.

eligibility.note: Anyone may enter. Asian stations work everyone; non-Asian stations score only contacts with Asian stations -- JARL: 'The points of completed contacts with Asian stations ... are shown below.' Not encoded as two_sided because that would need every Asian DXCC entity enumerated on both engines.

contests.exchange: RS(T) and the operator's age. An operator who does not want to send an age sends 01. Multi-operator stations send the average age of the operators at the start of the contest.
contests.source_note: jarl.org (67th All Asian DX Contest rule): 'Phone: (September 5-6, 2026) From 00:00 UTC on the first Saturday in September to 24:00 UTC on the following day'. The first Saturday in September 2026 is September 5, which is the date JARL prints. JARL's word is 'Phone'; recorded as SSB, the nearest term in this catalog's controlled mode set. Bands and power as for the CW leg. LOG DEADLINE DELIBERATELY NOT ENCODED, for the same reason as the CW leg: JARL's '10 days after the event is over' resolves to 'Phone...September 16, 2026', which is 9 days after the 24:00 UTC end instant stored here. Logs also go to aaph@jarl.org.
contests.summary: JARL's phone leg of the All Asian DX Contest: 24 hours over the first weekend in September, exchanging signal report and the operator's age.

eligibility.note: Anyone may enter. Asian stations work everyone; non-Asian stations score only contacts with Asian stations.

contests.name: JARL World Wide RTTY Contest
contests.exchange: RST and the operator's age; 01 (or 00 or 99) may be sent instead. Multi-operator stations send the average age of the operators.
contests.source_note: jarl.org (JARL World Wide RTTY Contest): 'From 00:00 UTC on the third Saturday in October to 24:00 UTC on the following day'. Mode: 'RTTY (Baudot only)'. Bands: '3.5, 7, 14, 21 and 28MHz'. Power: 'QRP: Total output power must not exceed 5 watts. Low Power: Total output power must not exceed 100 watts. High Power: The total output power must not exceed the maximum output power authorized for the station'. Log deadline: 'Logs must be submitted no later than 24:00 UTC on the 10th day after the end of the contest' -- which is exactly the stored end instant plus 10 days, so the number is encoded. The third Saturday in October 2026 is October 17. Logs also go to rtty@jarl.org.
contests.summary: JARL's worldwide RTTY contest: 24 hours over the third weekend in October, Baudot only, exchanging RST and the operator's age.

eligibility.note: 'This contest will be held for amateurs worldwide.' Same-continent contacts score 2 points, different-continent 3.

contests.name: New Year QSO Party
contests.exchange: RS(T) or a signal strength report plus the operator's name (a handle or initials is acceptable)
contests.note: BANDS UNRECORDED, NOT UNBANDED. Bands and modes: 'All bands and Modes permitted for JA amateur radio stations.' Exchange: 'RS(T) or signal strength report of the other station + operator's name (including handle name, initials, etc.)'. Contacts: 'JA stations: JA stations may contact any other stations. DX stations: DX stations may only contact JA stations.' Log deadline is a fixed date, 'January 31, 2026', not an interval, so log_deadline_days is omitted; logs go to nyp@jarl.org. Listed in JARL's own English contest index alongside All Asian DX and WW RTTY, which is why a QSO party is in this catalog at all.
contests.summary: JARL's new-year greeting party: five and a half days from January 2, all bands and modes, exchanging a report and the operator's name.

eligibility.note: 'All amateur radio stations and SWLs.' DX stations may only contact JA stations.

contests.name: RAC Canada Day Contest
contests.bands_note: 160, 80, 40, 20, 15, 10, 6 and 2 metres, CW and phone (SSB, FM, AM, etc.)
contests.exchange: Stations in Canada send RS(T) and province or territory; stations outside Canada, and Canadian maritime mobiles, send RS(T) and a serial number
contests.source_note: RAC Contest Rules 2026 (https://www.rac.ca/mivahih/2026/06/RAC_CanadaDayContestRules_2026.pdf, linked from https://www.rac.ca/contesting-results/): 'Contest Periods: RAC Canada Day Contest: Canada Day Wednesday, July 1, 2026 - 00:00:00 UTC to 23:59:59 UTC'. The contest is Canada Day, so the rule is the fixed date; the 2025 rules PDF says the same for 'Canada Day Tuesday, July 1, 2025'. Log deadline: 'all entries must be electronically submitted by 23:59 UTC 14 days after the end of the contest (July 15, 2026)' -- July 1 plus 14 days is July 15, so RAC's own arithmetic checks out and the interval is encoded. rules_url is RAC's stable results-and-rules hub rather than the year's PDF, whose path embeds the month it was uploaded. Logs also go to canadaday@rac.ca.
contests.summary: RAC's Canada Day contest: 24 hours on July 1, CW and phone from 160 to 2 metres, with Canadian stations sending their province.

eligibility.note: RAC: 'Amateurs all over the world are invited to join us in these celebrations.'

contests.name: RAC Canada Winter Contest
contests.bands_note: 160, 80, 40, 20, 15, 10, 6 and 2 metres, CW and phone (SSB, FM, AM, etc.)
contests.exchange: Stations in Canada send RS(T) and province or territory; stations outside Canada, and Canadian maritime mobiles, send RS(T) and a serial number
contests.note: RAC ANNOUNCES THIS DATE EACH YEAR; THERE IS NO RULE. The eight dates encoded here were read from RAC's own annual rules PDFs: 2019-12-28, 2020-12-19, 2021-12-18, 2022-12-17, 2023-12-30, 2024-12-28, 2025-12-20, 2026-12-27. That is the fourth, third, third, third, fifth, fourth and third Saturday of December -- and in 2026 a Sunday. No ordinal fits, so nothing is guessed: years RAC has not yet published are simply absent from this calendar.
contests.source_note: RAC Contest Rules 2026 (linked from https://www.rac.ca/contesting-results/): 'RAC Canada Winter Contest: Sunday, December 27, 2026 - 00:00:00 UTC to 23:59:59 UTC'. Earlier dates from RAC's own PDFs for each year; the 2019 rules even announce the next one, 'Next year the contest will be held on December 19, 2020.' Log deadline: 'all entries must be electronically submitted by 23:59 UTC 14 days after the end of the contest (January 11, 2027)'. DISCREPANCY RECORDED, NOT SILENTLY FIXED: December 27 plus 14 days is January 10, so RAC's parenthetical is one day later than RAC's own rule. The 14-day rule is what is encoded, because it is the rule; the Canada Day parenthetical in the same document checks out exactly. Logs also go to canadawinter@rac.ca.
contests.summary: RAC's winter contest: 24 hours on a December date RAC announces each year, CW and phone from 160 to 2 metres.

eligibility.note: RAC: 'Amateurs all over the world are invited to join us in these celebrations.'

contests.name: Remembrance Day Contest
contests.bands_note: Contacts may be made on MF (160M), HF and VHF & above bands except for WARC bands (10, 18 & 24MHZ) which are excluded by IARU agreement from all contest operations
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a serial number
contests.note: QRP entrants are limited to 5 watts average (CW/RTTY) or PEP (SSB) at the transmitter output. The band list is this catalog's reading of WIA's prose: the six HF/MF bands come from WIA's own SSB frequency list, 23cm/13cm/3cm from 'On 23cm or higher bands two points per completed valid contact', and 6m/2m/70cm from 'VHF & above'. 1.25m and 33cm are omitted because they are not Australian allocations.
contests.source_note: wia.org.au (Remembrance Day Contest rules): 'Weekend in August closest to the 15th, 0300 UTC Saturday to 0300 UTC Sunday.' Modes: 'Modes allowed are PHONE, CW and RTTY as per the era remembered.' Bands: the sentence quoted in bands_note, with SSB frequencies given as '1843-1875, 3535-3570 and 3600-3700, 7080-7300, 14112-14300, 21150-21450, 28300-29100KHz.' Logs: 'Submit Log WITHIN 14 DAYS by 0300z' via vklogchecker.com, or rdlogs@wia.org.au. The nearest-Saturday rule reproduces WIA's own published dates: August 15 2026 is itself a Saturday, and in 2023 the contest ran on August 12, the Saturday three days before Tuesday August 15.
contests.summary: The WIA's memorial contest for Australian amateurs who died in war: 24 hours from 0300 UTC on the August weekend nearest the 15th.

eligibility.note: WIA: 'Amateurs will endeavour to contact amateurs in VK call areas, ZL and P29 on all bands except WARC bands.' Contest teams may be formed from stations anywhere in VK, ZL or P2.

contests.name: John Moyle Memorial Field Day
contests.bands_note: 160, 80, 40, 20, 15, and 10 meters on HF and 50MHz to 241Ghz on VHF/UHF/SHF
contests.exchange: Single-operator and multi-single stations send RS(T) and a serial number starting at 001, running consecutively across all bands; multi-operator stations start a new series at 001 on each band
contests.note: A field day: WIA requires field stations to run from an independent power source, and 'Mains power operation of a portable station is expressly forbidden.' Power is not capped by the rules -- 'All entrants are to operate with power not to exceed their licence conditions for the mode and band of operation.'
contests.source_note: wia.org.au (John Moyle Memorial Field Day rules): 'The Field Day is held over the 3rd full weekend in March and run from UTC 0100 on the Saturday to 0100 on the Sunday.' Bands as quoted in bands_note. Modes: 'Phone (SSB AM FM)', 'CW', 'Mixed (both PH and CW modes)'. Exchange as quoted. Logs: 'within 14 days to vklogchecker dot com', or jmfd@wia.org.au. The third full weekend in March 2026 is March 21-22.
contests.summary: The WIA's portable-operation field day, honouring John Moyle: 24 hours from 0100 UTC on the third full weekend in March, HF through microwave.

eligibility.note: WIA: 'All stations are welcome to participate, but DX stations can only claim points for contacts with VK, ZL and P2 stations.'

contests.name: VK Shires Contest
contests.bands_note: 160 Metres, 80 Metres, 40 Metres, 20 Metres 15 Metres, 10 Metres. Please note there is 75m DX window permitted for VK stations
contests.exchange: VK stations send RS(T) and their VK shire abbreviation; stations outside VK send RS(T) and their CQ zone
contests.note: The recurrence is anchored to the second Monday of June -- a public holiday in most of Australia -- and the contest runs on the Saturday and Sunday before it, which is why the offsets are negative. Foundation and other QRP entrants have their own category at 10 watts.
contests.source_note: wia.org.au (VK Shires Contest rules): 'Held the Saturday and Sunday of the weekend prior to the second Monday of June every year.' and 'Starts: 00.00 UTC (10am EST)Saturday Ends: 00:00 UTC Sunday (10am EST)'. Bands and modes: 'B) Modes: SSB and CW only'. Exchange: 'All VK operators to exchange callsign, RS(T) followed by the VALID VK shire abbreviation as per the official list provided' and 'Stations outside VK to exchange callsign, RS(T) followed by CQ ZONE.' Logs: 'within 14 days of the end of the contest@ 0000 UTC' via vklogchecker.com. Checked against the dates WIA prints on the same page: the second Monday of June 2027 is June 14, so the weekend before is June 12-13, which is what WIA lists.
contests.summary: A hunt for Australian shires: 24 hours from 0000 UTC on the June weekend before the second Monday, with VK stations sending their shire.

eligibility.note: WIA: 'VK amateurs are to work the world including VK, whilst the rest of the world can only work VK'. To enter you must have worked at least one VK shire.

contests.name: Harry Angel Memorial Sprint
contests.bands_note: CW 3500 - 3535 kHz. Phone 3535 - 3700 kHz
contests.exchange: Callsign, RS(T) and a serial number starting at 001
contests.note: 106 minutes, one for each year of Harry Angel's life. WIA's page also prints 'This would make the next Saturday May 3rd May 2027' -- May 3 2027 is a Monday, and the first Saturday in May 2027 is May 1. This calendar follows the rule WIA states three times on the same page, not that sentence.
contests.source_note: wia.org.au (Harry Angel Memorial Sprint rules), which states the rule three times: 'The "HA" has been held on or around the first Saturday in May each year', 'For the last 27 years it has been held on the first Saturday in May each year.', and 'For the last 27 years the HA has been held on the first Saturday in May.' Times: '10:00 UTC - 11:46 UTC' and 'The duration of the contest is 106 minutes one minute for each year of Harry's life.' Sections: 'There will be three sections, PHONE, CW, MIXED'. Frequencies as quoted in bands_note. Exchange: 'Callsign,RS(T) and serial number commencing at 001'. Logs: 'all log entries must be submitted within 14 days of the start of the event' via vklogchecker.com or harryangel@redclifferadioclub.org.au. log_deadline_days is omitted because WIA measures those 14 days from the START of the sprint, not the end, which is not what this field means.
contests.summary: A 106-minute 80-metre sprint on the first Saturday in May, one minute for each year of Harry Angel's life.

eligibility.note: WIA: 'open to all amateurs in VK and ZL licensed to use 80m, including individual operators and stations representing radio clubs and societies'.

contests.name: Trans-Tasman Low-Band Contest
contests.bands_note: SSB voice transmission should be within 1843-1875, 3535-3570 and 3600-3700, 7080-7300KHz. Do not use voice in the digital section 3570-3600KHz
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a serial number starting at 001
contests.note: WIA runs one digital section covering PSK and RTTY, scored together. Both Digital and RTTY are recorded as modes because both are named in the rules, and a band-and-mode filter for either one should find this contest; PSK has no token in this catalog's vocabulary, so it sits in submodes.
contests.source_note: wia.org.au (Trans-Tasman Low-Band Contest rules): 'The contest is held on the Saturday night of the third full weekend of July.' and 'Start Time is 08:00 UTC and finish time is 14:00 UTC'. Bands: 'Bands: 160M 80M 40M'. Modes: 'Modes: SSB, CW and Digital (Digital includes PSK or RTTY only)' with 'PSK and RTTY are the only allowed digital modes and are combined, not counted separately.' Categories: 'Single Operator - High Power', 'Single Operator - Low Power (100 watts)', 'Single Operator - QRP*' with '* QRP stations are limited to 5 Watts average (CW/RTTY/PSK) or PEP (SSB) at the transmitter output.' Logs: 'LOGS ARE DUE WITHIN 8 DAYS OF CONTEST COMPLETION.' via vklogchecker.com or ttlogs@wia.org.au. The third full weekend of July 2026 is July 18-19, so the contest runs the evening of July 18.
contests.summary: Six hours across the Tasman on 160, 80 and 40 metres, on the Saturday night of the third full weekend in July.

eligibility.note: WIA: 'Amateurs in VK and ZL will endeavour to contact other amateurs in VK and ZL.'

contests.name: Oceania DX Contest, Phone
contests.bands_note: 160M, 80M, 40M, 20M, 15M and 10M (no WARC bands)
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a progressive serial number starting at 001
contests.note: The log deadline is announced each year rather than set as an interval -- 25 October in 2026, 31 October in earlier years -- so this calendar does not compute one. country is 'OC' because the sponsor is a joint VK/ZL committee rather than a national society; see data/sources.md.
contests.source_note: The recurrence in words comes from the WIA, a co-sponsor, at https://www.wia.org.au/members/contests/oceania/: 'PH - The first full weekend in October each year from 0600 UTC Saturday to 0600 UTC Sunday' and 'CW - The second full weekend in October each year from 0600 UTC Saturday to 0600 UTC Sunday.' Everything else is from the committee's own 2026 rules (https://www.oceaniadxcontest.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/ocdx26-rules-0.pdf, embedded at /rules): 'Phone Section: 06:00 UTC Saturday 3 October to 06:00 UTC Sunday 4 October 2026'; 'THE BANDS that can be used are 160M, 80M, 40M, 20M, 15M and 10M (no WARC bands)'; 'EXCHANGE: RS(T) report plus a progressive contact serial number starting at 001'; 'High power entrants must not exceed a total output power of 1500 Watts peak envelope power (PEP) ... Low power entrants must not exceed a total output power of 100 Watts PEP and QRP entrants must not exceed a total output power of 5 Watts PEP.' The rule reproduces the committee's own dates in both directions: the first full weekend of October is October 3-4 in 2026 and was October 5-6 in 2024.
contests.summary: Oceania's own international contest, phone leg: 24 hours from 0600 UTC on the first full weekend in October, when VK, ZL and the Pacific are the DX.

eligibility.note: Committee rules: 'There is no penalty for working non-Oceania stations but contacts between non-Oceania stations will score no points or multiplier credits.'

contests.exchange: RS(T) and a progressive serial number starting at 001

contests.name: Jock White Memorial Field Day
contests.exchange: RS(T), a serial number starting at 001, and an NZART branch number (home stations use 00)
contests.note: NZART SETS THIS ONE BY THE NEW ZEALAND CLOCK, NOT BY UTC: 1500-2400 Saturday and 0600-1500 Sunday NZDT. The UTC instants shown here therefore move with New Zealand daylight saving, unlike almost every other contest in this calendar. The QRP category is '5 Watts CW/10 Watts SSB maximum'; the 100W figure is NZART's overall limit. The log deadline is 'the Saturday which is four weeks after the Field Day Saturday' -- anchored to the Saturday rather than to either session's end -- so no interval is computed.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (Jock White Memorial Field Day rules): 'The last full weekend in February each year: on Saturday 1500-2400 NZDT and Sunday 0600-1500 NZDT. NOTE: when February only has three full weekends then field day will be held on Saturday 28th February and Sunday 1st March. This is to avoid a clash with the ARRL International CW contest. This will occur in 2026.' The exclusion is encoded exactly, not approximated: the last-full-weekend Saturday falls on February 21 if and only if February has 28 days and February 1 is a Sunday -- which is precisely the three-full-weekend case -- so exclude_dates [[2, 21]] pushes it to February 28 and reproduces NZART's own 2026 dates. 'Last Saturday in February' was tested and rejected: it diverges in a leap year beginning on a Saturday. Bands, modes and power: '40 and/or 80 metres, PHONE (SSB) and/or CW, 100 watts PEP maximum.' Exchange and log deadline as quoted in note.
contests.summary: NZART's branch field day: two evening-and-morning sessions on the last full weekend in February, 80 and 40 metres, run on New Zealand time.

eligibility.note: There is an entry category for 'Overseas stations in the Oceania Region', and contacts may be made 'with any other field, ZL home or overseas (Oceania) station'. In practice this is a New Zealand event with an Oceania fringe.

contests.name: NZART Sangster Shield
contests.exchange: New Zealand stations send RST, a serial number starting at 001 and their branch number; overseas stations send RST and a serial number
contests.note: A low-power contest by design, running since 1927: 'The output of the transmitter must not exceed 5 Watts PEP. Overseas contestants may use any power up to the maximum permitted by their license.' Three hours, worked as six half-hour periods. NZART moved to this one-night format for 2026.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (NZART Sangster Shield rules): 'Third Saturday of May each year, between the hours of 0800-1100 UTC (2000 NZST-2300 NZST) on Saturday evening. The maximum period of operation will be three hours (6 operating periods of 30 minutes each).' Times are stated in UTC, so unlike the Jock White Field Day this record is not wall-clock. Band: '80m'. Power as quoted in note. Exchange as quoted. Log deadline: 'on or before the fourth Saturday after the contest', which is exactly the stored end instant plus 28 days, so the interval is encoded; logs go to sangster@nzart.org.nz. Checked against the date NZART prints on the same page: 'The next Sangster Shield contest will be held on Saturday 16th May 2026', and the third Saturday of May 2026 is May 16.
contests.summary: NZART's oldest contest, a three-hour 5-watt CW event on 80 metres on the third Saturday evening in May.

eligibility.note: NZART: contacts count 'CW to CW between New Zealand stations and between New Zealand and overseas stations only' -- an overseas entrant can only work ZL.

contests.name: NZART Memorial Contest
contests.bands_note: Suggested frequencies CW 3520-3550 kHz, SSB 3610-3660 kHz
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a three-digit serial number starting at 001
contests.note: Held every year since 1946 for the New Zealand amateurs who died in the Second World War. Three one-hour periods; a station may be worked once per period on each of SSB and CW. The QRP category is '5W CW/10W SSB maximum'. The log deadline is a fixed date, 'Logs must arrive no later than 31 July', not an interval, so none is computed; logs go to contests@nzart.org.nz.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (NZART Memorial Contest rules): 'First Saturday in July each year 0800 - 1100 UTC (2000 - 2300 NZST) Three one-hour operating periods.' Band: '80m only - A station may be contacted twice during each operating period - once on SSB and once on CW'. Mode categories: 'Mixed mode - SSB and CW', 'CW only', 'SSB only'. Power: 'Open - 100W maximum CW/SSB' and 'QRP - 5W CW/10W SSB maximum'. Exchange as quoted. Checked against the date NZART prints on the same page: 'The next Memorial Contest date is Saturday 4th July 2026', and the first Saturday in July 2026 is July 4.
contests.summary: NZART's memorial contest for amateurs lost in the Second World War: three hours on 80 metres on the first Saturday evening in July.

eligibility.note: Multipliers are ZL, VK and Oceania prefixes, so the scoring is built around New Zealand and its neighbours.

contests.bands_note: Suggested frequencies CW 3520-3550 kHz
contests.exchange: RS(T) and the outside temperature to the nearest degree; on CW, 'm' denotes a minus sign
contests.note: One of three back-to-back 29-minute sprints on the same evening, each in a different mode and each scored separately, which is why they are three records here rather than one. Logs are due 'within 24 hours of the end of the sprint' -- shorter than a day, so no deadline interval is computed; they go to markzl3ab@gmail.com.

Band: '80m'. Categories: 'Single Operator, one transmitted signal only, use of the DX cluster is allowed and one of: 100w maximum (by convention Low Power in your contest logger); or QRP - up to 5W CW, 10W SSB and 5W FT4'. Exchange: 'CW/SSB RS(T) report and Outside Temperature to the nearest degree.' Scoring: 'Each mode will be scored separately.'
contests.summary: A 29-minute CW sprint on 80 metres every Tuesday evening in April and August, exchanging a report and the outside temperature.

contests.name: LABRE DX Contest
contests.bands_note: Only the 1.8, 3.5, 7, 14, 21, and 28 MHz bands may be used

contests.note: LABRE prints a log submission link, https://www.labre.org.br/sendlog, which returned 404 when this record was checked; entries can also be raised with contest@labre.org.br. No log_submit_url is recorded rather than one that does not resolve.

contests.source_note: oraricontest.id (Rules for outside Indonesia -- North Jakarta ORARI DX CONTEST): 'Time: Every June 2nd Weekend', 'Contest will start: 13 June 2026 -> 00:00 UTC - 23:59 UTC ( 24 Hours )'. Bands: 'Contact should made on 3.5, 7, 14, 21 and 28 MHz. No WARC bands.' Exchange: 'All Indonesia Stations : 5/9 + ORARI' and 'DX Stations outside Indonesia : 5/9 DX'. Log deadline: 'All logs must be sent within 7 (seven) days after the end of contest'. contests.summary: Indonesia's anniversary DX contest: 24 hours of SSB on the second June weekend, with YB stations as the multiplier everyone wants.

eligibility.note: ORARI: 'For amateurs around the world to contact as many other amateurs in as many countries and Indonesia ( YB Land ) stations. Everyone Worked Everyone'.

contests.name: Coupe du REF, CW
contests.exchange: French metropolitan stations send RS(T) + the number of the department where the antenna is located (e.g. 599 69); F6REF, the REF's official station, sends RS(T) + 00. DOM/TOM stations send RS(T) + the prefix of their entity (e.g. 599 FM). Foreign stations send RS(T) + a serial number starting at 001.
contests.source_note: concours.r-e-f.org, 'Championnat de France - « Coupe du REF », Premiere et deuxieme parties HF - telegraphie et telephonie', 1(b): 'Bandes HF (80-10 m) -- Dernier week-end entier du mois de janvier (telegraphie) ou fevrier (telephonie), du samedi a 0600 UTC au dimanche a 1800 UTC.' English rules, 2: 'CW: Last full weekend in January. SSB: Last full weekend in February. Contest Period: 36 hours each mode (separate contests). Starts 0600 UTC Saturday; ends 1800 UTC Sunday'. Bands and modes, English rules (reg_cdfhfdx_en_20260420.docx, 'French HF Championship "Coupe du REF" rules'): '80, 40, 20, 15, 10 m, according to IARU band plan for each country, CW and Phone.' Power classes, FR 2(c): 'Classe A (QRP) : la puissance est inferieure ou egale a 5 W, Classe B (LP) : la puissance est superieure a 5 W et inferieure ou egale a 100 W, Classe C (HP) : la puissance est superieure a 100 W.' Log deadline, FR 9: 'Comptes rendus au format Cabrillo a deposer sur la page de la commission des concours au plus tard huit jours apres la partie du concours disputee' -- EN 8: 'All log entries must be postmarked no later than 8 days after the contest' -- so log_deadline_days is 8. REF published 24-25 January 2026 and 25-26 January 2025 for the CW part; the last-full-weekend rule reproduces both.
contests.note: CONTRADICTION IN REF'S OWN DOCUMENT, RECORDED RATHER THAN RECONCILED: section 1(b) scopes these two parts to 'Bandes HF (80-10 m)' and the English rules list '80, 40, 20, 15, 10 m', but section 3(c) of the same PDF says 'Segments concours IARU des bandes 160, 80, 40, 20, 15 et 10 metres'. The document also governs the 160 m sub-part (REF 160 Metres, a separate record here), which is the likely reason the band is listed in 3(c); the 80-10 m reading is encoded because it is the one that scopes these parts specifically and the one the English rules repeat. REF's common HF rules ('Regles communes a tous les concours HF', 6A) state the deadline as '8 (huit) jours apres la fin du concours a minuit heure legale francaise', so the computed instant here is the end plus 8 days rather than French legal midnight.
contests.summary: The CW half of France's national HF championship: 36 hours over the last full weekend in January, 80 through 10 metres, French stations sending their department number.

eligibility.note: The rules define 'stations etrangeres' as 'Toute station ne repondant pas a la definition ci-dessus' and give them their own categories and rankings ('Classement par continent et par classe de puissance'), but 4(b) limits them to French contacts: 'Stations etrangeres -- Seules les liaisons avec des stations francaises sont valables.'

contests.name: REF 160 Metres
contests.exchange: RST + the French department number. French stations record only the serial number given by foreign stations.
contests.source_note: concours.r-e-f.org, 'REF 160 METRES -- REGLEMENT', 1: 'DATE ET HORAIRE -- Troisieme week-end de novembre, du samedi a 1700 UTC au dimanche a 0000 UTC.' 2: 'BANDE ET MODE -- 160 metres (1810 a 1850 KHz), CW uniquement.' 3: 'REPORTS -- RST + numero du departement. Les stations francais ne noteront que le numero de serie donne par les stations etrangeres, a l'exclusion de toute autre indication.' 7: 'COMPTES RENDUS -- Informatise, au format cabrillo.' 8: 'ENVOI -- A plus tard le deuxieme lundi apres le concours'. Power classes are 'selon definitions des regles communes HF', i.e. the same A/B/C classes as the Coupe du REF. REF published 21-22 November 2026 and 15 November 2025; the third-weekend rule reproduces both.
contests.note: log_deadline_days is derived, not quoted: REF words the deadline as 'le deuxieme lundi apres le concours' and states no hour. The contest ends at 0000 UTC on the Sunday, and that Sunday plus 8 days is the second Monday after the contest in every year, so 8 is exact for the date and silent about the time of day. WORDING DIFFERENCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN RECONCILED: this PDF says 'Troisieme week-end de novembre' while the Coupe du REF PDF, describing the same sub-part in section 1(a), says 'Troisieme week-end entier du mois de novembre'. The two readings cannot diverge -- the third Saturday of November is at most the 21st, so its Sunday is always in November -- so no choice between them was needed.
contests.summary: REF's top-band CW contest, Saturday evening into Sunday midnight UTC on the third weekend of November, French stations sending their department number.

eligibility.note: Section 5 scores 'Station etrangere contactant une station francaise', and section 5 (multipliers) gives foreign stations '1 par departement', so foreign entry is provided for and scored -- against French stations.

contests.name: DDFM 50 MHz
contests.exchange: French metropolitan stations send RS(T) + department + a six-character locator (e.g. 59 75 JN18DU); all other stations send RS(T) + serial number + locator (e.g. 59 001 KN04FG).
contests.source_note: concours.r-e-f.org, 'DDFM 50 MHz -- REGLEMENT', 2: 'DATE ET HORAIRE -- Le concours debute le deuxieme samedi de juin 1400 UTC et s'acheve le dimanche a 1400 UTC.' 3: 'FREQUENCES ET MODES -- SSB, CW, FM.' 4: 'ECHANGES -- Les stations francaises de metropole passent : RS(T) + Departement + QRA locator sur 6 caracteres ... Toutes les autres stations passent : RS(T) + numero de serie + QRA locator sur 6 caracteres'. 7: 'COMPTES RENDUS -- Informatise : compte-rendu au format IARU « reg1test ».' 8: 'ENVOI -- Au plus tard le premier mercredi qui suit le concours'. REF published 13-14 June 2026 and 14-15 June 2025; the second-Saturday rule reproduces both.
contests.note: FM is recorded as a submode because the catalog's mode vocabulary has no FM token; REF lists 'SSB, CW, FM' as the permitted modes and all three are worked on the same 6 m band. log_deadline_days is derived from 'le premier mercredi qui suit le concours': the contest ends 1400 UTC Sunday and the following Wednesday is exactly three days later, in every year. CONTRADICTION RECORDED RATHER THAN RECONCILED: REF's 2025 contest calendar listed this contest with a 15:00 start, while this rules PDF and REF's 2026 calendar both say 14:00. The rules are encoded. Separately, REF's 2026 calendar prints the 'Coupe du REF - OM complet' row with its end before its start (27/06/2026 06:00 to 07/06/2026 14:00); no record here depends on it.
contests.summary: REF's national 6-metre contest, 24 hours from the second Saturday of June, exchanging department or serial plus a six-character locator.

eligibility.note: Section 6 establishes 'Un classement F (toutes categories confondues). Un classement etranger.' -- a French ranking and a foreign ranking -- and section 4 gives foreign stations their own exchange format.

contests.name: UBA DX Contest, SSB
contests.exchange: Stations on Belgian territory send RS(T) + serial number starting with 001 + the abbreviation of their UBA section (e.g. 59001 ACC); non-members send XXX and the national stations send UBA. Stations outside Belgium send RS(T) + serial number starting from 001.
contests.source_note: uba.be/en/hf/contest-rules/uba-dx-contest, 'UBA DX Contest 2026', 2 - Periods: 'SSB - January 31 - February 1, 2026 (starts every year on the last Saturday of January).' and 'From 13:00 UTC on Saturday to 13:00 UTC on Sunday.' 4 - Bands: 'Bands to be used: 80, 40, 20, 15 and 10 meters.' 5 - Contest call and exchange as quoted in the exchange field. Power: 'High Power more than 100 Watts output. Low Power maximum 100 Watts output. QRP SSB maximum 10 Watts output, CW maximum 5 Watts output.' Deadline: 'The deadline for submitting logs is 7 days. For SSB 8 February 23:59 UTC / For CW 8 March 23:59 UTC'.
contests.note: LAST SATURDAY, NOT LAST FULL WEEKEND, and UBA's own 2026 dates are what settle it: 31 January 2026 is a Saturday and 1 February is a Sunday, so the last full weekend of January 2026 would be 24-25 January. UBA published 31 January - 1 February, which only the last-Saturday reading produces. The QRP figure recorded here is the SSB one; UBA's rule is 'QRP SSB maximum 10 Watts output, CW maximum 5 Watts output.' The stated deadline instants (SSB 8 February 23:59 UTC, CW 8 March 23:59 UTC) are the right dates for a 7-day interval but 23:59 rather than the 13:00 that end-plus-7-days gives; the interval is what UBA states as the rule, so it is what is encoded.
contests.summary: Belgium's national DX contest, phone leg: 24 hours from 1300 UTC on the last Saturday of January, with UBA section abbreviations as multipliers.

eligibility.note: Categories exist for 'Stations with QTH in Belgium' and 'Stations with QTH outside Belgium', and the 39th EUROPEAN UNION TROPHY goes to the highest-scoring EU member station. UBA adds a standing exclusion: 'until further notice, radio amateurs from the Russian Federation and Belarus will be excluded from participation.'

contests.name: UBA PSK63 Prefix Contest
contests.exchange: Stations outside Belgium send RSQ + a serial number starting with 001; stations in Belgium send RSQ + the three-letter code of their UBA section (non-members send XXX, the national stations send UBA).
contests.source_note: uba.be/en/hf/contest-rules/uba-psk63-prefix-contest, 'UBA PSK63 Prefix Contest 2027', 1. Date: '9 january 2027, 12:00 UTC until 10 january 2027, 11:59 UTC. (every year the 2nd weekend of january)'. 2. Participants: 'Participation is open to all radio amateurs world wide in possession of a valid licence and to all SWL's.' 3. Mode and bands: 'BPSK63 only / 10, 15, 20, 40 and 80 meter, in the segments recommended by the IARU for this mode.' 4. Power: 'Maximum power output 50 W (5 W for QRP), in order not to cause interference or splatter to other participants.' 14. Logs: 'The logs must be sent no later than one week after the contest. The final submission deadline is January 17, 2027, 23:59 UTC.' UBA's own contest calendar independently gives the 2026 edition as 10/01/2026 12:00 to 11/01/2026 12:00; the second-weekend rule reproduces both years.
contests.note: The stated deadline instant (17 January 2027 23:59 UTC) is the right date for the seven-day interval UBA states but 23:59 rather than the 11:59 that end-plus-7-days gives. The interval is the rule, so the interval is encoded. Nothing distinguishes 'the 2nd weekend of january' from 'the second full weekend' in either published year, so the full-weekend form is used and no claim is made that UBA meant one rather than the other.

The PDF words the 2026 period as a date only: 'From 14 February 2026 1200 UTC until 15 February 2026 1200 UTC'. 3.1 Contest bands and segments: 'These are 160m, 80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m'. 6.2: 'Dutch (PA) stations: signal report + province code (two letters)'. 12.1: 'Logs must be submitted to the contest sponsors before February 20 23:59 UTC 2026. ATTENTION: THE LOG SUBMISSION PERIOD IS 5 DAYS!' VERON independently published three further editions -- 13-14 February 2027, 12-13 February 2028 and 10-11 February 2029 -- and the second-full-weekend rule reproduces all three.
contests.note: The stated deadline instant (20 February 23:59 UTC) is the right date for the five-day period VERON states but 23:59 rather than the 12:00 that end-plus-5-days gives; the interval is what the rules call the rule, so the interval is encoded. As of 2026-08-18 veron.nl's rules link still served the 2026 edition while the site's front page advertised 2027.

Contest Period -- second weekend in April, i.e. 1200 UTC 11 April - 1159 UTC 12 April 2026'. 'All bands, 1.8 through 28 MHz, WARC bands excluded'. '5.1 Non-Czech and Slovak stations: signal report + QSO number, starting with 001. / 5.2 Czech and Slovak stations: signal report + County code (three letters).' '11.1 Logs must be submitted to the contest sponsors within 7 days after the end of the contest .. (APRIL 19, 2026, 2359 UTC)'.
contests.note: The parenthetical deadline (19 April 2026, 2359 UTC) is the right date for the seven-day interval but 23:59 rather than the 11:59 that end-plus-7-days gives; the interval is the stated rule, so the interval is encoded. WORDING DIFFERENCE, RECORDED RATHER THAN RECONCILED: the SSB rules say 'second weekend in April' where the CW rules say 'Second (full) weekend in November'. The two readings cannot diverge at n = 2 -- the second Saturday of a month is at most the 14th, so its Sunday is always in the same month -- so no choice between them was needed. BLOCKER RECORDED, NOT WORKED AROUND: okomdx.crk.cz serves a TLS certificate issued for default.web4u.cz, so HTTPS fails validation and the rules are reachable only over plain HTTP. rules_url is therefore http:// deliberately; it is not an oversight, and the link checker will keep reporting it as such until the Czech Radio Club fixes the host.

contests.name: WAE DX Contest CW
contests.exchange: RS/RST + serial from 001. QTC traffic scores additional points: a QSO already logged is reported back to a European station as time, callsign and serial, at most 10 between any two stations, and each correctly passed QTC counts a point to both ends.
contests.source_note: darc.de/der-club/referate/conteste/wae-dx-contest/regeln/ (Ausschreibung, Stand 2025-06-17): 'Der Deutsche Amateur Radio Club (DARC) lädt alle Funkamateure weltweit zum jährlich stattfindenden WAEDC-Contest ein.' -- 'DARC invites all radio amateurs worldwide to the annual WAEDC contest.' Bänder: '3,5 - 7 - 14 - 21 - 28 MHz.' Kontrollziffernaustausch: 'Ausgetauscht werden RS/RST und eine Seriennummer ab 001.' -- 'RS/RST and a serial number from 001 are exchanged.' Einsendeschluss, Punkt 13: 'Der Einsendeschluß ist immer 7 Tage nach dem Contest.' -- 'the deadline is always 7 days after the contest.' Wettbewerbszeiten: 'CW: August, zweites Wochenende. Samstag, 8. August 2026, 0000 UTC bis Sonntag, 9. August 2026, 2359 UTC' -- 'CW: August, second weekend. Saturday 8 August 2026, 0000 UTC to Sunday 9 August 2026, 2359 UTC.' Ruhepausen: 'Während des 48 Stunden dauernden Contests dürfen Einmannstationen nur 36 Stunden arbeiten.' -- single operators may work only 36 of the 48 hours. Verified 2026-08-18.
contests.note: DARC states the deadline twice as an interval and once as an instant, and for the CW leg the instant disagrees. Rule 13 says 'immer 7 Tage nach dem Contest' and the general contest rules say the same; seven days from this leg's end is 16 August 2026, which is the date DARC's own KW contest calendar prints. The per-leg line on the same rules page reads 'Einsendeschluss CW: 17.08.2026, 23:59 UTC', a day later. The interval is what is encoded -- it is stated twice, and it reproduces the printed instants of the SSB and RTTY legs exactly. Both statements are recorded here rather than reconciled.

eligibility.note: 'Der Deutsche Amateur Radio Club (DARC) lädt alle Funkamateure weltweit ... ein.' Scoring is one-sided: 'Ein Wettbewerbs-QSO kann nur zwischen einer europäischen und einer außereuropäischen Station geführt werden' -- a contest QSO can only be made between a European and a non-European station. Not encoded as two_sided, which would need DARC's whole WAE country list enumerated in both engines; same call as JARL All Asian.

contests.exchange: RS/RST + serial from 001. QTC traffic scores additional points; in the RTTY leg every station may send and receive QTCs, at most 10 between any two stations, but the QTC exchange itself must cross continents.
contests.source_note: darc.de/der-club/referate/conteste/wae-dx-contest/regeln/ (Ausschreibung, Stand 2025-06-17): 'Der Deutsche Amateur Radio Club (DARC) lädt alle Funkamateure weltweit zum jährlich stattfindenden WAEDC-Contest ein.' -- 'DARC invites all radio amateurs worldwide to the annual WAEDC contest.' Bänder: '3,5 - 7 - 14 - 21 - 28 MHz.' Kontrollziffernaustausch: 'Ausgetauscht werden RS/RST und eine Seriennummer ab 001.' -- 'RS/RST and a serial number from 001 are exchanged.' Einsendeschluss, Punkt 13: 'Der Einsendeschluß ist immer 7 Tage nach dem Contest.' -- 'the deadline is always 7 days after the contest.' Wettbewerbszeiten: 'RTTY: November, zweites Wochenende. Samstag, 14. November 2026, 0000 UTC bis Sonntag, 15. November 2026, 2359 UTC' -- 'RTTY: November, second weekend.' Punkt 12, Spezielle Regelungen für RTTY: 'Im RTTY-Teil des WAEDC entfällt die Kontinentbeschränkung; jeder kann jeden arbeiten. Nur der QTC-Austausch muss zwischen verschiedenen Kontinenten abgewickelt werden.' -- 'in the RTTY part the continent restriction does not apply; everyone can work everyone. contests.name: DARC Weihnachtswettbewerb (XMAS Contest)
contests.exchange: German stations send RS(T) + their DOK, or 'NM' if they are not a DARC or VFDB member. All stations outside Germany send RS(T) + serial number.
contests.source_note: darc.de/der-club/referate/conteste/weihnachtswettbewerb/regeln/: 'Der Deutsche Amateur-Radio-Club (DARC) lädt alle Funkamateure zur Teilnahme am jährlichen Weihnachtswettbewerb (XMAS-Contest) ein.' '1. Termin: 26. Dezember, 08.30-10.59 UTC.' -- '26 December, 0830-1059 UTC.' DARC's own English page states the same: 'XMAS, 26. December 2026, 8.30-10.59 UT.' Betriebsarten und Bänder: 80m and 40m, 'CW 3510-3560 khz 7010-7040 khz, SSB 3610-3650 3700-3775 khz 7060-7100 7130-7200 khz'; 'Es sind maximal 20 Wechsel der Betriebsart oder des Bandes während der gesamten Contestzeit zugelassen.' -- at most 20 band or mode changes in the whole contest. Logeinsendeschluß: 'NEU: 7 Tage nach dem Wettbewerb (für den Contest 2026 der 2.01.2027)' -- 'NEW: 7 days after the contest.' Verified 2026-08-18.
contests.note: A calendar-fixed date, not a weekday rule: 26 December whatever day it falls on. DARC shortened the log deadline to seven days and flags the change itself ('NEU: verkürzte Logabgabefrist auf 7 Tage').
contests.summary: Boxing-morning sprint on 80 and 40 metres, two and a half hours long, with a twenty-change cap that makes band planning part of the game.

eligibility.note: 'Der Deutsche Amateur-Radio-Club (DARC) lädt alle Funkamateure zur Teilnahme ... ein' -- DARC's own English page renders it 'has the honor to invite all radio amateurs to participate in the annual XMAS Sprint-Contest.'

contests.name: DARC FT4 Contest
contests.bands_note: 80m 3576, 3579 and 3582 kHz USB; 40m 7047.5 kHz USB
contests.exchange: Signal report + four-character grid square (for example JN49, JO61).
contests.source_note: darc.de/der-club/referate/conteste/ft4-contest/ft4-rules/: 'Veranstalter: DARC Referat Conteste. Termin: Jeweils 2. Monat im Quartal, Am 2. Dienstag im Monat' -- 'organiser: DARC contest department. Date: the second month of each quarter, on the second Tuesday of the month.' The dates DARC lists beside it are 10.02.2026, 12.05.2026, 11.08.2026 and 10.11.2026, all 19:00-20:29 UTC. 'Bänder: 80m (3576, 3579 und 3582 kHz USB), 40m (7047.5 kHz USB). Betriebsarten: FT4.' 'Austausch: Signal Report und Locator-Großfeld (z. Bsp.: JN49, JO61).' 'Betrieb im Fox-Modus ist nicht erlaubt.' -- fox mode operation is not permitted. 'Einsendeschluss: jeweils 7 Tage.' Verified 2026-08-18.
contests.note: Four legs a year, one record. DARC heads its 2026 date list 'Termine 2025:' -- the heading is a year out, the dates under it are 2026 and match DARC's KW contest calendar, so the typo is in the heading only.
contests.summary: Quarterly ninety-minute FT4 sprint on 80 and 40 metres, with an annual standing split between low power and QRP. Fox mode is barred.

eligibility.note: 'zu arbeitende Stationen: alle, jede Station einmal pro Band'; 'Getrennte Wertung für DL- und Non-DL-Stationen' -- everyone may be worked, once per band, and German and non-German entries are scored separately.

contests.name: DARC RTTY-Kurzcontest
contests.exchange: RST + DOK; German non-members send 'NM'. Stations outside Germany send RST + serial from 001.
contests.source_note: darc.de/der-club/referate/conteste/rtty-kurz/rtty-rules/: 'Veranstalter: DARC Referat Conteste. Termin: jeweils im 1. Monat eines jeden Quartals am 2. Dienstag' -- 'date: in the first month of each quarter, on the second Tuesday.' The dates DARC lists beside it are 13.01.2026, 14.04.2026, 14.07.2026 and 13.10.2026, all 18:00-19:29 UTC. 'Bänder: 80m, 40m. Betriebsarten: RTTY (45,45 Baud).' 'Austausch: RST und DOK. Nichtmitglieder geben statt eines DOK "NM". Alle Stationen außerhalb DL: RST und eine laufende Nummer, beginnend mit 001.' 'Einsendeschluss: jeweils 7 Tage nach Contestende.' The landing page states the purpose: 'Zur Pflege und Erhaltung der Betriebsart RTTY im Amateurfunkdienst schreibt der Deutsche Amateur Radio Club e.V. einen Jahreswettbewerb über insgesamt vier Kurzconteste in der Betriebsart RTTY aus.' -- to maintain and preserve RTTY, DARC runs an annual competition over four short contests. Verified 2026-08-18.
contests.note: Four legs a year, one record, offset one month from the FT4 contest: RTTY takes the first month of each quarter and FT4 the second, both on the second Tuesday.
contests.summary: Ninety minutes of RTTY on 80 and 40 metres, four times a year, scored into an annual standing so a single missed leg costs little.

eligibility.note: 'Zu arbeitende Stationen: alle, jede Station einmal pro Band'; 'Getrennte Wertung für DL- und Non-DL-Stationen' -- everyone may be worked, once per band, and German and non-German entries are scored separately.

contests.name: Helvetia Contest
contests.exchange: Swiss stations send RS(T) and their canton abbreviation (59 ZH, 599 ZH); stations outside Switzerland send RS(T) and a serial number of at least three digits.
contests.source_note: uska.ch Reglement fuer den Helvetia-Wettbewerb, Ausgabe Maerz 2026. 2.1 Datum und Zeit: 'Letztes volles Wochenende im April, Samstag 13:00 UTC bis Sonntag 12:59 UTC.' (Last full weekend in April, Saturday 13:00 UTC to Sunday 12:59 UTC.) 2.4 Baender: '160 m, 80 m, 40 m, 20 m, 15 m und 10 m'. 2.5.1 Schweizer Stationen: 'Rapport (RS oder RST) und dem Kanton (z.B. 59 ZH, 599 ZH)'; 2.5.2 auslaendische Stationen: 'Rapport (RS oder RST) und der laufenden, mindestens dreistelligen Verbindungsnummer'. 2.7 gives 10 points for a QSO with Switzerland, 1 within one's own continent and 3 to another continent; multipliers are cantons plus DXCC entities per band. 2.9 requires a six-hour rest taken in at most two periods. Power: 'High Power 1000 Watt, Low Power 100 Watt', QRP 'CW maximal 5 Watt / SSB maximal 10 Watt / Fuer digitale Betriebsarten maximal 5 Watt'. Digital is defined in the Reglement: 'Digital - Damit sind Modes wie RTTY, PSK31, PSK63, FT4 und FT8 gemeint. Cabrillo Tag fuer RTTY = RY, bzw. PSK31, PSK63, FT4 und FT8 = DG' (Digital means modes such as RTTY, PSK31, PSK63, FT4 and FT8; the Cabrillo tag for RTTY is RY, and DG for PSK31, PSK63, FT4 and FT8). 11 Log: 'Die Logs sind innert 8 Tagen zwingend ueber das webbasierte User-Interface auf der USKA-Website einzureichen: https://contestlog.uska.ch.' Entry is open beyond Switzerland: the Reglement says the contest is 'in der Schweiz und im Ausland ausgeschrieben' (announced in Switzerland and abroad). USKA's own KW-Contest page (uska.ch/kw-contest/) prints the 2026 dates separately from the Reglemente: Helvetia 25.-26. April, Field Day 6.-7. Juni and 5.-6. September, NMD 19. Juli, Weihnachtswettbewerb 5. und 12. Dezember. Every one of them is reproduced by the encoded rule.
contests.note: The last full weekend of April, encoded as n=-1: April 2026 has full weekends on the 4th/5th, 11th/12th, 18th/19th and 25th/26th, so the rule gives 25-26 April, which is what USKA's own KW-Contest page prints. USKA also prints 24-25 April 2027 there, and the rule reproduces that too. Operators must take a six-hour rest in at most two periods; the record carries the full 24-hour window because that is when the contest is on air.
contests.summary: Switzerland's national DX contest over the last full weekend of April. Cantons are the multiplier, so Swiss stations are worth chasing on every band, and CW, SSB and digital each count separately.

eligibility.note: The Reglement states the contest is 'in der Schweiz und im Ausland ausgeschrieben' -- announced in Switzerland and abroad -- and 2.5.2 gives foreign stations their own exchange, so anyone may enter.

contests.name: USKA Field Day (CW)
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a serial number of at least three digits. With fixed stations the report alone is enough.
contests.source_note: uska.ch Reglement fuer den Field Day, Ausgabe Mai 2026. 2.1 Datum und Zeit: 'CW: Erstes volles Wochenende im Juni, Samstag 15:00 UTC bis Sonntag 14:59 UTC. / SSB: Erstes volles Wochenende im September, Samstag 13:00 UTC bis Sonntag 12:59 UTC.' (CW: first full weekend in June, Saturday 15:00 UTC to Sunday 14:59 UTC; SSB: first full weekend in September, Saturday 13:00 UTC to Sunday 12:59 UTC.) 1.3 Standort: 'Der Standort muss sich in der Schweiz befinden.' (The location must be in Switzerland.) 2.5 Kontrollaustausch: RS(T) plus a serial of at least three digits -- 'Bei Verbindungen mit festen Stationen genuegt der RS/RST-Rapport (ohne Verbindungsnummer)'. Points: 2 for a fixed station in Europe, 3 outside, 4 for a portable station in Europe and 6 outside; portable means /p, /m, /mm or /am. 11 Log: 'Die Logs sind innert 8 Tagen zwingend ueber das webbasierte User-Interface auf der USKA-Website einzureichen: https://contestlog.uska.ch.' Entry notice is due by 12:00 UTC on the Friday before. USKA's own KW-Contest page (uska.ch/kw-contest/) prints the 2026 dates separately from the Reglemente: Helvetia 25.-26. April, Field Day 6.-7. Juni and 5.-6. September, NMD 19. Juli, Weihnachtswettbewerb 5. und 12. Dezember. Every one of them is reproduced by the encoded rule.
contests.note: One of USKA's two Field Day legs; they share a Reglement and differ only in month, mode and start time, so they are two records. The first full weekend of June 2026 is 6-7 June and of September 2026 is 5-6 September, both of which USKA's KW-Contest page prints.
contests.summary: USKA's CW Field Day: 24 hours from a Swiss location, with portable stations worth double the points of fixed ones.

eligibility.note: 1.3 of the Reglement: 'Der Standort muss sich in der Schweiz befinden.' Stations elsewhere are worked and scored by the entrants but cannot enter themselves.

contests.name: USKA National Mountain Day (NMD)
contests.bands_note: CW in 3510-3560 kHz and SSB in 3600-3650 kHz.
contests.exchange: Between NMD stations, RS(T) and a text of at least 15 characters that may be used only once. With everyone else, the report alone.
contests.source_note: uska.ch Reglement fuer den National Mountain Day, Ausgabe Mai 2026. 4 Datum und Zeit: 'Dritter Sonntag im Juli, 06:00 UTC bis 09:59 UTC.' (Third Sunday in July, 06:00 UTC to 09:59 UTC.) 2 Betriebsarten: 'Zulaessige Betriebsarten sind CW und SSB. CW-Verbindungen sind im Bandsegment 3510 - 3560 kHz abzuwickeln. SSB-Verbindungen sind im Bandsegment 3600 - 3650 kHz abzuwickeln. Dem Rufzeichen muss der Zusatz /P angehaengt werden. ... Remote-Betrieb ist nicht zulaessig.' 3 Standort: 'Der Standort muss sich in der Schweiz befinden und mindestens 800 m ueber Meer liegen.' 6b Gewicht: 'Die gesamte Stationseinrichtung darf hoechstens sechs Kilogramm wiegen' -- no mains power and no pre-existing antennas. 9 Bewertung: 4 points for a QSO with an NMD station, 1 for any other. Logs go to nmd@uska.ch within 8 days; entries must be registered by the Tuesday before at nmd.uska.ch/anmeldung. USKA's own KW-Contest page (uska.ch/kw-contest/) prints the 2026 dates separately from the Reglemente: Helvetia 25.-26. April, Field Day 6.-7. Juni and 5.-6. September, NMD 19. Juli, Weihnachtswettbewerb 5. und 12. Dezember. Every one of them is reproduced by the encoded rule.
contests.note: USKA splits the four hours into halves (06:00-07:59 and 08:00-09:59) only to allow one repeat QSO per mode with each NMD station; it is one continuous contest and is encoded as one span. The third Sunday of July 2026 is the 19th, which is the date USKA's KW-Contest page prints.
contests.summary: Four hours of 80m from a Swiss summit above 800 m, carrying everything you need in six kilos. Non-NMD stations are worked for a point and need send only a report.

eligibility.note: 3 of the Reglement: 'Der Standort muss sich in der Schweiz befinden und mindestens 800 m ueber Meer liegen.' Anyone may be worked; only stations on a Swiss summit can enter.

(SSB: first Saturday in December; CW: second Saturday in December, both 07:00-09:59 UTC; Digital: first and second Saturday in December, 10:00-10:59 UTC.) 2.4 Baender: '80 m und 40 m'. 2.5 Kontrollaustausch: RS(T) and the canton abbreviation. Eligibility: 'Der Weihnachtwettbewerb wird fuer Funkamateure sowie Empfangsamateure in der Schweiz ausgeschrieben' and 'Der Standort muss sich in der Schweiz befinden.' PSK31, PSK63, FT4 und FT8 = DG' (Digital means modes such as RTTY, PSK31, PSK63, FT4 and FT8; the Cabrillo tag for RTTY is RY, and DG for PSK31, PSK63, FT4 and FT8). Juli, Weihnachtswettbewerb 5. und 12. Dezember. Every one of them is reproduced by the encoded rule.
contests.note: USKA runs the Weihnachtswettbewerb on two Saturdays, and each Saturday is a phone-or-CW morning followed by a separate digital hour. This record is the first Saturday: SSB 07:00-09:59 UTC and digital 10:00-10:59 UTC, encoded as two sessions because the hour between them is not part of the contest. The two Saturdays are two records because they are different modes, not two legs of one event. The first Saturday of December 2026 is the 5th and the second the 12th, the dates USKA's KW-Contest page prints. USKA states no log deadline in this Reglement -- the other three KW Reglemente all say 'innert 8 Tagen' and this one says nothing at all -- so no interval is encoded rather than one borrowed from its siblings.
contests.summary: USKA's Christmas contest on 80m and 40m: a SSB morning on the first Saturday of December, then a digital hour. Cantons are the exchange.

contests.name: All Austrian Exercise AOEE 80/40m
contests.exchange: RS(T) and the Austrian Bezirkskenner (district identifier).
contests.source_note: oevsv.at Regeln AOEE 80/40m 2026 (PDF). '2. TERMIN: 1. Mai 2026'. '3. ZEIT: 1. Periode 0500 - 0800 UTC entspricht 0700 - 1000 MESZ / 2. Periode 1400 - 1700 UTC entspricht 1600 - 1900 MESZ' (1st period 0500-0800 UTC = 0700-1000 CEST; 2nd period 1400-1700 UTC = 1600-1900 CEST). 1 Teilnahmeberechtigt: stations transmitting from Austria, including guest and CEPT licences. 4 Frequenzen: CW 3.510-3.560 and 7.000-7.040 MHz; SSB 3.600-3.650, 3.700-3.800 and 7.060-7.100, 7.130-7.200 MHz. 5 Betriebsarten: CW und SSB. 7 Kontrollnummer: RS(T) plus Bezirkskenner. 9 Klassen: LP up to 100 W, HP over 100 W, plus MIX and Newcomer. 14 Einsendeschluss: '08. MAI 2026 23:59 Uhr MESZ'. Second source, published separately by OEVSV: the HF-Referat page says 'Unter anderem wird die Notfunk-Uebung All Austrian Exercise AOEE 80/40m am 1. Mai ... durchgefuehrt.'
contests.note: An emergency-communications exercise run as a contest, on a fixed calendar date rather than a weekend rule. Two periods with six hours between them, encoded as sessions. The log deadline is a stated instant -- 8 May 2026, 23:59 CEST -- and not an interval from the end of the contest (the second period ends 17:00 UTC, and seven days later is 19:00 CEST), so it is recorded here rather than as log_deadline_days.
contests.summary: Austria's May Day emergency-communications exercise on 80m and 40m, run in a morning and an afternoon period with districts as the exchange.

eligibility.note: Section 1 limits entry to stations transmitting from Austria, including holders of guest and CEPT licences operating there.

contests.name: All Austrian 160m Contest (AOEC 160m)
contests.bands_note: 1810-2000 kHz in the German rules; the English rules say 1810-1950 kHz. Both are OEVSV's own statements and neither has been withdrawn.
contests.exchange: RST and a serial number; Austrian stations add their OE district identifier.
contests.source_note: oevsv.at Regeln AOEC 160m (PDF, 2025 Ausschreibung). '3. TERMIN: Jeweils am dritten vollen Wochenende im NOVEMBER / Samstag 1600 UTC bis 2359 UTC / 15. November 2025' (Every year on the third full weekend in November, Saturday 1600 UTC to 2359 UTC). OEVSV's English edition of the same rules states the same rule independently: 'PERIOD: Third full weekend each November / Saturday 1600 - 2359 UTC'. Teilnahmeberechtigt: 'alle ... lizensierten Funkamateurinnen und -amateure sowie SWLs weltweit' (all licensed amateurs and SWLs worldwide). Betriebsart: CW only. Kontrollnummer: RST plus serial, with OE stations adding their district.
contests.note: The third full weekend of November is a rule OEVSV states twice, in German and in English, and it reproduces the date the German edition prints for itself: November 2025's full weekends are the 1st/2nd, 8th/9th and 15th/16th, so the third is Saturday 15 November 2025. For 2026 the 1st is a Sunday whose Saturday belongs to October, so the full weekends start on the 7th/8th and the rule gives Saturday 21 November 2026. CONTRADICTIONS, recorded not reconciled: the German rules say 1810-2000 kHz and the English 1810-1950 kHz; the German rules take logs at aoec-auswertung.oevsv.at and the English at contestrobot.aoec160m.oevsv.at, so neither is encoded as the log_submit_url. The deadline is a fixed date (30 November), not an interval. BLOCKER: OEVSV's HF-Referat page still offers only the 2025 Ausschreibung, so this is the current published document and it is on the pending list to re-read.
contests.summary: Austria's worldwide 160m CW contest: eight hours from 1600 UTC on the Saturday of the third full November weekend, with OE districts as the prize.

eligibility.note: 'Teilnahmeberechtigt sind alle ... lizensierten Funkamateurinnen und -amateure sowie SWLs weltweit' -- all licensed amateurs and SWLs worldwide.

contests.name: HA-DX Contest
contests.exchange: Hungarian stations send RS(T) and their county abbreviation; everyone else sends RS(T) and an incremental serial number.
contests.source_note: ha-dx.com/en/contest-rules, MRASZ's own rules page. '1. Organizer: Magyar Radioamator Szovetseg (www.mrasz.hu).' '3. Date and time: every year 3rd full weekend of January, from Saturday 12:00 UTC to Sunday 12:00 UTC. In 2026: 17-18 January.' '4. Participants: every amateur radio operator in the world'. '6. Modes: A1A morse code (CW) and A3J phone (SSB).' Bands 160, 80, 40, 20, 15 and 10 m. Exchange: HA stations send RS(T) and county, others RS(T) and a serial. Points: 10 for a Hungarian station, 2 within one's own continent, 5 to another; /AM and /MM are worth 2. Categories QRP up to 5 W, LP up to 100 W, HP above. 'Log submission deadline: Logs must be uploaded on the HA-DX website within 5 days of the end of the contest.'
contests.note: MRASZ states the rule and the year in the same sentence, which is its own check: January 2026's full weekends are the 3rd/4th, 10th/11th, 17th/18th and 24th/25th (31 January's Sunday falls in February), so the third is 17-18 January -- the date the rules print. The contest ends at 12:00 UTC, not 11:59, so the Sunday overlaps the Saturday start by a minute; that is what the rules say.
contests.summary: Hungary's international DX contest over the third full weekend of January. Hungarian counties are the multiplier and HA stations are worth ten points.

eligibility.note: '4. Participants: every amateur radio operator in the world'.

contests.name: HA YL-OM Contest
contests.exchange: RS, the age of the licence in years and the operator's first name -- for example '59 01 Kata'.
contests.source_note: ylom.mrasz.hu/yl-om-versenykiiras. 'Ideje: minden evben marcius 8-hoz legkozelebb eso hetvegen, 2026. marcius 08. vasarnap / URH 13.30-14.30 UTC / RH 14.30-16.00 UTC' (Held every year on the weekend nearest to 8 March; in 2026 Sunday 8 March, VHF 13:30-14:30 UTC and HF 14:30-16:00 UTC). Bands: 80 m SSB 3.600-3.720 MHz; 2 m SSB 144.150-144.390 and FM 145.250-145.575 MHz except 145.500. 'Kontrollszam: RS + az adoengedely kora ... + az operator keresztneve. Pl: 59 01 Kata' (RS + the age of the licence + the operator's first name). Points: 5 for a YL-OM or YL-YL QSO, 1 for OM-OM. 'Hatarido: a versenyt koveto 15. nap (hetfo)' (deadline: the 15th day after the contest, a Monday). 'Resztvevok: Hazai es magyarul beszelo kulfoldi radioamator' (participants: Hungarian and Hungarian-speaking foreign amateurs), and QSOs are conducted in Hungarian.
contests.note: MRASZ ties the date to International Women's Day: the weekend nearest 8 March, run on the Sunday. Encoded as the Sunday nearest 8 March, which gives 8 March 2026 -- the date MRASZ prints -- because 8 March 2026 is itself a Sunday. Only that one year is independently confirmed, so the rule is recorded as MRASZ's wording rather than as a tested multi-year pattern. contests.name: LZ DX Contest
contests.exchange: Stations outside Bulgaria send RS(T) and their ITU zone; LZ stations send RS(T) and a two-letter district abbreviation.
contests.source_note: lzdx.bfra.bg/rulesen.html, the Bulgarian Federation of Radio Amateurs' own rules. 'The weekend before the last full weekend of November (the weekend before CQWW CW contest weekend) from 12:00 UTC on Saturday till 11:59 UTC on Sunday (22-23 November 2025). Logs due 0000Z, Dec 7 2025'. Bands: '80, 40, 20, 15 and 10 meters ... on both CW and SSB modes.' Exchange: non-LZ stations send RS(T) and ITU zone, LZ stations RS(T) and their two-letter district. contests.note: 'The weekend before the last full weekend of November' is a rule, not an annual announcement -- BFRA anchors it to CQ WW CW, which sits on the last one -- so it is encoded as n=-2 and this is the record that made the engine count backwards past 'last'. November 2025's full weekends are the 1st/2nd, 8th/9th, 15th/16th, 22nd/23rd and 29th/30th, so n=-2 gives 22-23 November, the date BFRA prints. For 2026 it gives 21-22 November. contests.summary: Bulgaria's DX contest, deliberately placed the weekend before CQ WW CW. LZ stations are worth ten points and hand out districts.

eligibility.note: The rules give an exchange for stations inside and outside Bulgaria and score QSOs by continent, with no entry restriction.

contests.name: YO DX HF Contest

contests.exchange: Stations outside Romania send RS(T) and a serial from 001; YO stations send RS(T) and their county abbreviation.

Date and Time: The contest is held during the fourth full weekend of August: Saturday 12:00:00 UTC - Sunday 11:59:59 UTC (24 hours).' Romanian edition: 'Al patrulea weekend intreg al lunii August: / Sambata 12:00:00 UTC - Duminica 11:59:59 UTC (24 de ore in total).' 4.1 restricts operation to 3.5-28 MHz excluding the WARC bands. 5.1: non-YO stations send RS(T) and a serial from 001; 5.2.1: YO stations send RS(T) and their county. 6: 8 points for a YO station, 4 to another continent, 2 within one's own continent, 1 within one's own DXCC entity, and YO-YO contacts score 0. 12.1: 'All logs must be submitted to the contest organizers within 7 (seven) days from the end of the competition.' CONTRADICTION, recorded not reconciled: an older FRR rules PDF on hamradio.ro says 'Ultimul weekend intreg al lunii August' (the LAST full weekend of August), which would give 29-30. The current yodx.ro rules and FRR's own 2026 announcement agree on the fourth, so that is what is encoded. Observation: the Romanian page leaks '[cite: 9]' markers into its text, which suggests it was assembled by a tool; the wording still matches the English edition.

contests.name: Croatian DX Contest (9A DX)

contests.name: ES Open HF Championship
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a continuous serial number from 001.

(The competition is held in 9 stages on Saturday mornings according to ERAU's calendar plan.) 4.3: 'Etappide algus on 10:00 Eesti aja (EA) jargi ja lopp 11:00 EA' with four periods, the last running 10:45-10:59 EA. 4.4: modes CW and SSB on 80 m, CW below 3600 kHz and SSB above, 3530-3560 and 3600-3650 kHz recommended. 4.5: up to 100 W, QRP 10 W. 4.6: exchange RS(T) and a continuous serial from 001; CW scores 2 points and SSB 1. 7: logs are due 'hiljemalt voistlusele jargneva nadala neljapaeval kella 09.59'ks (EA)' -- by 09:59 Estonian time on the Thursday of the following week. Second source, published separately by ERAU: its 2026 calendar lists all nine dates -- 03.01, 14.02, 07.03, 04.04, 02.05, 05.09, 03.10, 07.11 and 05.12 -- and prints their UTC windows as 08:00-08:59 for stages 1, 2, 3, 8 and 9 and 07:00-07:59 for stages 4, 5, 6 and 7.

The rules give no date rule at all -- 4.2 defers to the calendar plan -- so the dates are manual and taken from ERAU's published 2026 calendar. Eight of the nine are the first Saturday of their month; February's is the second. The log deadline is 'the Thursday of the following week', which is not a fixed number of days from the end of each stage, so it is recorded here rather than as log_deadline_days. contests.name: Vytautas Magnus Contest (VMC)

contests.exchange: RS(T), a serial number from 001 and a six-character WW locator.
contests.source_note: lrmd.lt/vmc/, the Lietuvos radijo megeju draugija's own rules. 'Varzybos vyksta kiekvienais metais pirma sekmadieni po Nauju metu, 0700-0759 UTC. Artimiausia data: 2026-01-04, 0900-0959 LST.' The English text on the same page: 'The contest takes place annually on the first Sunday after New Year's Day, from 0700 to 0759 UTC.' Modes 'CW, SSB, FM'; bands 80 m (3510-3600 CW, 3600-3700 SSB) and 2 m (144.050 CW, 144.300 SSB, 145.500 FM). 'Dalyvauti gali visi licencijuoti Lietuvos ir uzsienio radijo megejai (isskyrus Rusija ir Baltarusija)' (all licensed Lithuanian and foreign amateurs may take part, except Russia and Belarus). 'Ne daugiau kaip 100 W.' Exchange: 'RS(T) + rysio eiles numeris nuo 001 + 6 zenklu WW lokatorius'. One point per QSO; the multiplier is distinct WW locators per band. 'Ataskaitas siusti per 24 valandas po varzybu pabaigos' (send logs within 24 hours of the end). Logs to VMC@QRZ.LT in LYtest format; paper logs are not accepted.
contests.note: Encoded as the first Sunday in January, which gives 4 January 2026 -- the date LRMD prints. CAVEAT: LRMD's two wordings diverge in the years when 1 January is itself a Sunday. 'The first Sunday AFTER New Year's Day' would then be the 8th, while the first Sunday IN January is the 1st. No such year has been published by LRMD, so neither reading can be tested against a sponsor date; the first-Sunday reading is encoded and the divergence recorded rather than resolved. FM is in submodes because it is not in the catalog's mode vocabulary.

'Daznai: 3530-3600 kHz CW ir 3600-3700 kHz SSB/CW', with 3600-3610 kHz reserved for mobile CQ calls. 'Spinduliuotes galia: ne daugiau 100 W.' 'Dalyviai: Lietuvoje ir kitose salyse licenzijuoti radijo megejai ir stebetojai, isskyrus dalyvius is saliu agresoriu, t.y. Rusijos Federacijos ir Baltarusijos Respublikos.' 'ataskaitos CABRILLO formatu turetu buti issiustos, ne veliau kaip per dvi savaites po varzybu, elektroniniu pastu walcontest@lrmd.lt'

contests.name: Portugal Day Contest (HF)
contests.bands_note: 10, 15, 20, 40 and 80 meter bands, fully respecting licensing rules of each country. Observance of established band plans is strongly encouraged.
contests.exchange: DX stations send RST and a sequential number beginning 001; Portuguese stations, including the Azores and Madeira, send RST and the letters identifying their district (or county in the Azores and Madeira).
contests.source_note: concursos.rep.pt/portugal-day-contest-hf/ and portugaldaycontest.rep.pt/rules.php, REP's own rules in English: 'REP – Rede dos Emissores Portugueses, sponsors ‘PORTUGAL DAY CONTEST’ each year on the second weekend of June, being part of IARU Contest Calendar. All radio amateurs of the world are welcome to participate!' Time: '12:00 UTC to 11:59 UTC'. Bands: '10, 15, 20, 40 and 80 meter bands'. Mode: 'SSB, CW or Mixed'. Exchange: 'DX Stations send RST followed by one sequential number beginning 001. Portuguese Stations (including Autonomous Regions of Azores and Madeira Islands) send RST followed by letters identifying their respective District (or County if Azores and Madeira Islands)'. Logs: 'Logs should be organized following Cabrillo file format.' 'All entries must be emailed or postmarked no later than June 30th of the same year to: e-mail to rep-concursos@rep.pt'. The Portuguese page regras_hf.php states the same rule: 'A REP Rede dos Emissores Portugueses, organiza no 2º fim de semana de junho de cada ano, o Concurso Dia de Portugal' -- the 2nd full weekend of June each year. REP publishes six years of dates independently of the rule, and the second full weekend of June reproduces all six: Jun 14-15 2025, Jun 13-14 2026, Jun 12-13 2027, Jun 10-11 2028, Jun 9-10 2029, Jun 8-9 2030.
contests.note: log_deadline_days is deliberately absent. REP states a fixed calendar deadline -- 'no later than June 30th of the same year' -- not a span, and June 30 is 15 days after the 2025 running but 16 after the 2026 one, so any single number would be wrong in most years. REP's 2030 date is what pins the recurrence, and it rules out the reading that would otherwise be tempting: 1 June 2030 is itself a Saturday, so a reader who did not count a weekend opening on the 1st would make 8-9 June the first and 15-16 the second. REP publishes 8-9 June, so the weekend opening on the 1st counts. Nothing turns on full weekend versus second Saturday here -- the two readings give the same date in every year from 2025 to 2060, because only a Saturday falling on a month's LAST day fails to open a full weekend, which a second Saturday never is. The full-weekend type is encoded because 'fim de semana' is REP's own wording, not because it changes an answer. 'Mixed' is one of REP's three entry categories rather than a fourth mode -- the contest permits SSB and CW, which is what modes records. Logs go to rep-concursos@rep.pt by e-mail; there is no submission website, so log_submit_url is absent.
contests.summary: Portugal's national DX contest: 24 hours from 1200 UTC on the second June weekend, with Portuguese districts and Azores and Madeira counties as multipliers alongside DXCC entities.

eligibility.note: 'All radio amateurs of the world are welcome to participate!' -- REP's own wording.

contests.name: Concurso Dia de Portugal VHF/UHF
contests.bands_note: As recomendadas nos planos de banda da IARU, Região 1, (2m=144MHz; 4m=70 MHz; 70cm=432MHz; 23cm=1200MHz e 13cm=2300 MHz) -- the IARU Region 1 band plans. REP's list includes 4m (70 MHz), which is not in this catalog's band vocabulary and so is recorded here rather than in bands.
contests.exchange: Callsign, RS(T), a number beginning 001 and the full QTH locator (for example IM58is). The log must also carry the UTC time and the date of each contact.
contests.source_note: concursos.rep.pt/concurso-dia-de-portugal-vhf-uhf/, REP's own rules: 'A Rede dos Emissores Portugueses, organiza no 10 de junho (feriado) de cada ano o Concurso “Dia de Portugal de VHF-UHF”' -- organised on 10 June, the public holiday, each year. '3 - Período do Concurso: 10 de junho das 12H00 às 18H00 UTC.' Participants: 'Podem participar todos os radioamadores devidamente licenciados' (all properly licensed radio amateurs may take part). Modes: '5 - Modos: Fonia e CW.' Exchange: 'Cada operador em Fonia ou CW passará o Indicativo, controle de sinal RS(T), número a começar por 001 e QTH Locator completo (exemplo-IM58is). No log é obrigatório reportar QTR (Hora/UTC) e a data correspondente ao contacto.' Logs: '9 - Formato dos LOGs: Preferencialmente em formato “Cabrillo”, uma folha log por banda.' '10 - Envio de LOGs: Devem ser enviados até 20 de junho.' REP ran it on 10 June 2025, a Tuesday: its own 'Logs recebidos - VHF-UHF 2025' post is dated 10 June 2025 and opens '10 de junho de 2025'.
contests.note: REP PUBLISHES TWO CONTRADICTORY RULES FOR THIS CONTEST AND BOTH ARE LIVE. concursos.rep.pt, the portal linked from rep.pt's own front page, says 10 June every year, lists 2m/4m/70cm/23cm/13cm, weights points per band and sets the log deadline at 20 June. portugaldaycontest.rep.pt/regras_vhf_uhf.php still says 'no 2º Sábado do mês de junho de cada ano, (8 de Junho de 2024)', lists only 2m/70cm/23cm, and sets the deadline at 30 June. The two disagree about the date in every year where 10 June is not the second Saturday. The fixed date is encoded because it is the one REP actually ran: 10 June 2025 was a Tuesday and REP's logs-received post for the 2025 running is dated that day, whereas the second Saturday of June 2025 was the 14th. The superseded page is recorded here rather than silently ignored. Because both the contest and the deadline are fixed dates, log_deadline_days is exactly 10 in every year -- unlike REP's two other contests, whose deadlines are calendar dates that do not sit a constant span after the contest. Modes: REP writes 'Fonia' (phone) rather than SSB specifically; SSB is the catalog's only phone token.
contests.summary: REP's VHF and UHF contest, run on Portugal Day itself: six hours from 1200 UTC on 10 June, scored on distance between QTH locators with grid squares as the multiplier.

eligibility.note: 'Podem participar todos os radioamadores devidamente licenciados' -- all properly licensed radio amateurs may take part.

contests.source_note: concursos.rep.pt/concurso-rep-50-mhz/, REP's own rules: '2. Período: Primeiro fim de semana completo de agosto, desde as 14:00 UTC de sábado às 14:00 UTC de domingo. 2025: o concurso ocorre nos dias 2 e 3 de agosto.' -- the first COMPLETE weekend of August, 1400 UTC Saturday to 1400 UTC Sunday. Scope: '3. Âmbito Internacional. São válidos os contactos efetuados por estações devidamente licenciadas', and 'Este concurso está aberto a todos os radioamadores devidamente licenciados.' Band: '5. Banda: 6 m (50 MHz)'. Modes: '6. Modos de emissão: Fonia (AM, SSB, FM) e/ou telegrafia (CW).' Exchange: 'o controle de sinal RS(T); Número sequencial de QSO, começando em 001; QTH Locator (exemplo: IM58is), de ambas as estações.' Logs: 'Os ficheiros de log a enviar no só formato Cabrillo', sent to rep-concursos@rep.pt. REP's own 2025 date confirms the rule: 1 August 2025 was a Friday, so the first full weekend of August 2025 is 2-3 August, which is what REP prints.
contests.note: REP writes 'fim de semana completo' -- complete weekend -- which is exactly the distinction this engine models: a Saturday/Sunday pair with both days inside the month. It is encoded because it is REP's wording, NOT because it changes a date: checked rather than assumed, the full-weekend and first-Saturday readings agree for the first weekend of August in every year from 2025 to 2060, because the only Saturday that can fail to open a full weekend is one falling on the month's last day. The distinction bites on 'last weekend' rules, not on this one. log_deadline_days is absent because REP states a dated deadline for the edition ('até às 23:59 (UTC) do dia 8 de Agosto de 2025') rather than a span, and 8 August is 5 days after the 2025 running but would be 6 after the 2026 one. Modes: REP allows phone as AM, SSB or FM; SSB is the catalog's only phone token, so AM and FM are recorded in submodes. REP has published no 2026 edition on concursos.rep.pt as of 2026-08-19, and the first full weekend of August 2026 has passed; the rule is encoded as REP states it and no suspension is inferred from a missing post.

FT4 and FT8 as Digital modes: The default frequencies for FT4 and FT8 in WSJT-X for the three contest frequencies of 20m, 40m and 80m.' Exchange: '5.2. FT4 and FT8 minimally a signal strength report and RRR/73/RRR73 and a serial number in each direction between the two parties.' Checked against SARL's own published dates as well as its rules: SARL publishes SARL-Contests-2026-Calendar.ics on the same page, whose times carry TZID="South Africa Standard Time" (a fixed +0200, no DST -- its own X-CALSTART confirms 09:00 local as 07:00Z). (1) SARL'S OWN TWO PAGES DISAGREE. The rules section says the contest starts '22:01 UTC 4 June (00:01 CAT) Thursday 4 June', but 22:01 UTC on Thursday 4 June is 00:01 CAT on FRIDAY 5 June. SARL's Date Ordered List resolves it: the start is Wednesday 3 June at 22:01 UTC, which is 00:01 CAT on Thursday 4 June. The date table is self-consistent and the prose is not, so the table is what is encoded.

(2) 'THE FIRST FULL WEEK OF JUNE' HAS TWO READINGS THAT DIVERGE NEXT YEAR. If a full week is a Monday-to-Sunday wholly inside June, then in 2027 -- when 1 June is a Tuesday -- the first full week is 7-13 June and the Thursday is the 10th. If it means the first week containing the whole Thursday-to-Sunday block, the Thursday is the 3rd. The two agree in 2026 and differ in 2027, so no ordinal rule is encoded: only the date SARL published. Years SARL has not announced are absent rather than guessed. Ask SARL which reading is intended and this becomes a rule.

contests.note:
VERIFIED FALSE, AND THE EXCEPTION IS THIS CATALOG'S INFERENCE RATHER THAN TRAC'S WORDING.

TRAC states 'Temmuz ayının ilk hafta sonu' -- the first weekend of July -- and that reproduces its own published dates for 2024, 2025 and 2026. It does NOT reproduce 2023: 1 July 2023 was itself a Saturday, so the rule gives 1-2 July, and TRAC ran the contest on 8-9 July, a week later.

`exclude_dates: [[7, 1]]` is what makes all FOUR published dates come out right, and it is the same shape as ARRL RTTY Roundup's 'first full weekend of January but never 1 January'. The difference is that ARRL states its exception and TRAC does not, so this is one year's evidence fitted into a rule rather than a rule read off a page.

It only matters when 1 July is a Saturday, which next happens in 2028, then 2034 and 2045. In every other year the exception is inert and the record is simply TRAC's own sentence. Ask TRAC what happens when the month opens on a Saturday and this becomes verified either way.

Modes: TRAC permits SSB, CW and FM. SSB is this catalog's only phone token, so FM is recorded in submodes and the ban on digital modes is in bands_note.

From 10:00 UTC to 13:00 UTC on Saturday 31 October 2026 (Last Saturday of October). The dates are three weeks after the RAE Radio Amateur Examination.' Frequency: '3. FM mode on the 6m, 2 m and 70cm bands'. Contacts: '4.1. Contacts must be two-way point to point. Stations shall exchange signal reports as well as their full six-digit Maidenhead locator.' '4.6. No EME, repeater, satellite or IRLP (Echo link etc.) contacts are allowed.' Eligibility: '1.6. The Contest is open to all licensed Radio Amateurs in South Africa, Namibia (V5), Botswana (A2), Zimbabwe (Z2), Mozambique (C9), Lesotho (7P) and ESwatini (3DA). Only contacts with these states will count.' Both dates are confirmed by SARL's own Date Ordered List and its SARL-Contests-2026-Calendar.ics.
contests.note:
THE RECORD THAT PUT FM IN THE MODE VOCABULARY. This contest is FM ONLY, and until 2026-08-19 this catalog had no FM token -- it used SSB as a general phone token, which was serviceable while every phone contest also allowed SSB. Recording an FM-only contest as SSB would have stated something SARL does not permit, which is precisely the overstatement the mode rules exist to prevent, so FM was added to CATALOG_MODES in both engines and to the filter families instead. Ten records that had been carrying FM in submodes moved it into modes in the same commit.

Two legs on one record: both run 10:00-13:00 UTC and differ only in their anchor, and the anchors are different SHAPES -- the second Saturday of June and the LAST Saturday of October -- which a composite holds without trouble.

SARL explains the timing: 'The dates are three weeks after the RAE Radio Amateur Examination', which is why the contest is aimed at newly licensed amateurs. That is context rather than a rule; the ordinals are what is encoded.

No log deadline was read in this pass, so none is recorded.
contests.summary: Three hours of FM on 6 m, 2 m and 70 cm, run twice a year three weeks after South Africa's licence exams, with grid squares exchanged.

eligibility.note: 'The Contest is open to all licensed Radio Amateurs in South Africa, Namibia (V5), Botswana (A2), Zimbabwe (Z2), Mozambique (C9), Lesotho (7P) and ESwatini (3DA). Only contacts with these states will count.' SARL names the prefixes itself here, so unlike its club contests this list is not an inference.
